confirmed: S1-O1 to S1-O3 are ratings of the written Product Improvement Task solutions. Two trained raters, blind to condition, scored each dimension from 1 to 5, and the final score is the mean of the two raters. Raters, not participants, gave the scores, so the outcomes are scored on the output and are not self-reports (PDF pp. 6-7, printed pp. 381-382, Sect. 3.4.1).

AI was available while the scored output was produced. Participants proposed the solutions 'using the assigned GAI tool' in a split screen, with the AI chat on the left and the document workspace on the right. Both tasks in both orders used an AI tool, and no AI-free task exists. No construct is diversity, so question with_ai follows the codebook rule (PDF pp. 6-7, printed pp. 381-382, Sect. 3.3 and 3.4.1; PDF p. 6, Fig. 2; PDF p. 8, Fig. 3).

Constructs hold. The paper defines quality as 'the extent to which a solution addresses the task objective' (usefulness), elaboration as 'the amount of detail provided' (elaboration), and originality as 'the novelty of the idea' (novelty). The paper measures no variety within one person and no similarity across people, so no flexibility or diversity outcome is missing (PDF p. 7, printed p. 382, Sect. 3.4.1).

Measure human_raters holds. The paper calls the raters 'trained' and says nothing about domain expertise, so expert_raters (domain experts, instructors, or professionals) does not apply. The reconciled forms c072, c077, c094, and c167 code trained raters without stated expertise the same way (PDF p. 7, printed p. 382, Sect. 3.4.1).

Unit participant holds. Sect. 3.5 describes the data as the students' creative performance in both GAI conditions and compares the conditions with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, which pair each student's two scores in the within-subject design. Table 2 correlates creative performance with self-efficacy and eye-tracking, which are measured once per student per condition. The quality r = .42 gives the printed p = .001 only at N = 62 (Z = 3.31, p = .0009). At 186 solution pairs, p would be about 1e-8 (PDF p. 8, printed p. 383, Sect. 3.5 and 4.1; PDF p. 10, printed p. 385, Table 2).

Reported numbers match Sect. 4.1 exactly. Quality: personalized 3.50 (SD 1.00) vs standard 3.08 (SD 1.12), p = .001, r = .42. Elaboration: 3.58 (SD 1.17) vs 2.48 (SD 1.04), p < .001, r = .62. Originality: 2.92 (SD 1.15) vs 3.13 (SD 1.27), p = .098, r = .18. The text prints no Z, SE, CI, or n with these results (PDF p. 8, printed p. 383, Sect. 4.1).

Fig. 4A agrees with the text. Measured in pixels against the y-axis ticks of the embedded image, the whisker centers read 3.08 and 3.50 (quality), 2.48 and 3.58 (elaboration), and 3.13 and 2.92 (originality), standard first. The half-spans read 1.12, 1.00, 1.04, 1.17, 1.27, and 1.15, equal to the printed SDs. The stars are ** for quality, *** for elaboration, and none for originality (PDF p. 9, printed p. 384, Fig. 4A).

The measure_detail fields match the source: inter-rater alpha 0.88 for quality, 0.90 for elaboration, and 0.86 for originality; solutions shown to raters in randomized order; final score the mean of the two raters. The paper does not say how the three solutions per task were combined, as the form notes (PDF p. 7, printed p. 382, Sect. 3.4.1).

Arms and directions hold. Both tools run on GPT-4. The treatment is the personalized tutor Mr. Ranedeer and the control is standard ChatGPT-4, so the contrast is ai_design. Quality and elaboration are higher under the treatment, and the paper reports 'No significant difference' for originality, which fits no_clear_difference (PDF p. 5, printed p. 380, Sect. 3.2.1; PDF p. 8, printed p. 383, Sect. 4.1).

No outcome is missing. The other measures are creative self-efficacy (four self-rated items on a 7-point scale), eye-tracking fixation duration and gaze transitions, and the within-condition correlations in Table 2. None is scored on the output. The paper reports no diversity measure and no task done after AI was removed (PDF p. 7, printed p. 382, Sect. 3.4.2 and 3.4.3; PDF p. 9, Table 1; PDF p. 10, Table 2).

The printed originality r and p disagree, as the form's open question says: r = .18 gives p = .16 at N = 62, and p = .098 gives r = .21. The form records the printed values unchanged, which is right for the reported field (PDF p. 8, printed p. 383, Sect. 4.1).
summary: The three c041 outcomes (quality, elaboration, and originality of the Product Improvement Task solutions) are scored by two trained raters blind to condition on output produced with AI available, and the form codes their question, construct, measure, unit, and numbers correctly against Sect. 3.4.1, Sect. 4.1, and Fig. 4A. No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing, so the conclusion stands and criterion 3 holds.
